Commentary.Commentary: The umpires and the players are taking their place on the field to start the second innings. New Zealand chasing 227 in 34 overs. David Willey to start the attack for England. Finn Allen and Devon Conway are the opening batters for New Zealand. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

As we eagerly await the second innings, New Zealand will be chasing a target of 227 in their allotted overs. The question on everyone's mind is whether the Kiwis can chase it down smoothly or if the English bowlers have some tricks up their sleeves. The stage is set for an exciting chase, so stay tuned for what promises to be a thrilling second innings.

The New Zealand bowlers, led by Trent Boult who picked up 3 wickets in his first 3 overs itself, struck early blows, dismissing England's top four during the powerplay. He marked his 100th ODI in fine fashion. However, they struggled to break partnerships in the middle overs as they were lacking wicket-taking deliveries in the middle overs, allowing England to rebuild. Despite tight fielding and restricting runs in the death overs, New Zealand managed to limit England to 226, a chasable target within the 34-over timeframe.

The first innings of the 2nd ODI between England and New Zealand was a rollercoaster ride under challenging conditions. England, batting first, faced an early collapse, losing four wickets for just 28 runs. Jos Buttler and Moeen Ali steadied the ship with a 48-run partnership until Buttler fell to Mitchell Santner. Then, it was the Liam Livingstone show as he blazed his way to an unbeaten 95 off just 78 balls with 9 boundaries and 1 six, forming a crucial 112-run partnership with Sam Curran, who contributed with 42 off 35. England posted a competitive total of 226/7 in their allotted 34 overs, all thanks to Livingstone's heroics.

Another couple of runs to end the innings then! Tim Southee serves another full toss, on middle, Liam Livingstone whips it towards deep square leg again and just makes it back for the second run in the end. England finish on 226/7!

Trent Boult has been absolutely brilliant in his 100th ODI while the spinners are now trying to build on that. Moeen Ali is looking in good touch and the host doesn't have much time to rebuild as this is a shortened game. So, Ali and Liam Livingstone will hope to change gears quickly. Also, Mitchell Santner to bowl after the break.

Commentary.Commentary: We are finally set to start! The sun is out and the two umpires are making their way out in the middle followed by the New Zealand players who spread out to take their respective field positions. Jonny Bairstow and Harry Brook are the two openers for England. Trent Boult who is playing his 100th ODI has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Jos Buttler, the captain of England says that they would have bowled first as well. Adds that they want to play with more intensity as they are known for that. Says Dawid Malan misses out after the birth of his second child. Informs they have made three changes as well.

Tom Latham, the skipper of New Zealand says that they will bowl first. Adds that it is because of the weather later on and they will look to chase here. Tells that they put on a fine show in the previous game and will look to back it up with another good performance here. Informs they have made three changes.

England (Playing XI) - Jonny Bairstow (In place of Dawid Malan), Harry Brook, Joe Root, Ben Stokes, Liam Livingstone, Jos Buttler (C)&(WK), Moeen Ali (In place of Moeen Ali), Sam Curran (In place of Chris Woakes), David Willey, Gus Atkinson, Reece Topley.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Finn Allen (In place of Henry Nicholls),​​​​ Devon Conway, Will Young, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Latham (C)&(WK), Glenn Phillips, Rachin Ravindra, Mitchell Santner (In place of Kyle Jamieson), Matt Henry, Tim Southee, Trent Boult (In place of Lockie Ferguson).
The coin lands in favour of Tom Latham and New Zealand have elected to BOWL first.
